questions.stem: What do we call an animal or plant that has died out everywhere on Earth?
options: endangered
extinct
protected
migrating
questions.explanation: Extinct means no longer living anywhere on Earth, and it can never come back. Endangered means in danger of becoming extinct.

questions.stem: Cutting down forests is called ___. Harmful things put into the air or water are called ___.
questions.explanation: Deforestation destroys the homes of animals such as elephants. Pollution includes smoke, rubbish, plastic and dirty water.

questions.stem: Match each way of caring for the environment to an example.
pairs: take a cloth bag to the market
use an old tin as a pencil pot
take newspapers to the paper collector (bhangari)
switch off lights and fans when you leave a room
questions.explanation: Reduce means use less, reuse means use again, and recycle means make used materials into new things. Saving energy and not littering help too.

questions.stem: Sort these actions into those that help the environment and those that harm it.
questions.explanation: Planting trees, using cloth bags and cleaning up help living things. Plastic in rivers, hunting and wasting electricity cause harm.

questions.stem: There are far more people in Bangladesh today than long ago, so our actions can have a bigger effect on living things.
questions.explanation: Today there are more than 170 million people in Bangladesh. We use more land, water and wood, so what we do matters more.

questions.stem: Which of these harm the environment? Choose all that are right.
options: filling in wetlands to build roads
pouring dirty factory water into rivers
planting trees in the monsoon
catching too many young fish
making a national park
questions.explanation: Filling wetlands, polluting rivers and overfishing harm living things. Planting trees and making national parks protect them.

questions.stem: Why is it a problem to catch too many young fish?
options: Fishing nets get damaged.
The remaining fish grow too large.
Young fish are too small to taste good.
Not enough fish grow up to breed.
questions.explanation: Young fish that are caught cannot grow up and have babies, so the number of fish falls. Laws protect fish while they breed.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to show how plastic litter can harm a sea animal.
sequence: A plastic bag is dropped on the street.
Rain washes it into a drain.
The drain carries it to a river and then the sea.
A turtle mistakes it for food and eats it.
questions.explanation: Plastic does not rot, so litter flows from drains to rivers and the sea, where turtles and dolphins can mistake it for food.

questions.stem: Before 2002, many thin plastic bags were used in Dhaka. What problems did they cause?
questions.model_answer: The thin plastic bags blocked the drains, and this made floods worse.
questions.explanation: Plastic does not rot. Thin plastic bags blocked drains and made floods worse in Dhaka, so Bangladesh banned them in 2002.

questions.stem: A plastic bottle left on the ground can take how long to break down?
options: hundreds of years
about one whole year
only a few weeks
around ten years
questions.explanation: Plastic breaks down very slowly, so one bottle can stay in the environment for hundreds of years.

questions.stem: The Sundarbans is protected as a wildlife ___, where animals can live safely.
questions.explanation: National parks and wildlife sanctuaries such as the Sundarbans and Lawachara protect habitats.

questions.stem: In Bangladesh, people plant millions of trees every year during the ___.
questions.explanation: Planting trees during the wet monsoon helps them grow. Trees give homes and food to animals and help to protect the soil.

questions.stem: Taking a cloth bag to the market is an example of recycling.
questions.explanation: Taking a cloth bag means you use fewer plastic bags, so it is an example of reducing. Recycling means making used materials into new things.

questions.stem: Which action saves electricity at home?
options: leaving the light on in an empty room
keeping the television on all day
switching off the fan when you leave
running the fan with nobody in the room
questions.explanation: Switching off lights and fans when you leave a room uses less electricity.

questions.stem: Why is it important to tell other people about caring for the environment?
questions.model_answer: Many people acting together make a much bigger difference than one person.
questions.explanation: One person can make a difference, but many people together can make a big difference. You can talk to your family or start an eco-club.

questions.stem: Which picture shows a way to **help** the environment?
questions.explanation: A reusable bag lets you use fewer plastic bags. Factory smoke, car exhaust and oil spills pollute the air and water.

questions.stem: Sort these pictures into things that help the environment and things that harm it.
questions.explanation: Recycling, reusable bags, planting and putting litter in bins help. Smoke, oil spills and exhaust fumes pollute.

questions.stem: Match each picture to what it does.
pairs: makes used materials into new things
questions.explanation: Pollution harms living things. Planting trees and recycling help them.

questions.stem: Plastic in rivers flows to the sea. Which of these animals can mistake plastic for food? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Turtles and dolphins live in the sea and can mistake floating plastic for food. Deer and parrots do not live in the sea.

questions.stem: Cutting down forests destroys the homes of animals such as elephants. Which picture shows an animal that loses its home?
questions.explanation: Elephants live in forests, so they lose their food and shelter when forests are cut down. Whales, sharks and goldfish live in water.

questions.stem: At break time, Nadia sees sweet wrappers all over the school playground. What is the best action?
options: Sweep them into the nearest drain with a broom.
Wear gloves, pick them up and put them in a bin.
Leave them where they are for the wind to blow away.
Burn them in a pile behind the school building.
questions.explanation: Litter should go in a bin. Sweeping it into a drain blocks the drain and burning it pollutes the air. Gloves protect hands from dirt and sharp things.

questions.stem: The class litter survey shows that sweet wrappers are the most common litter. Which action fits this evidence best?
options: Plant more trees near the school gate.
Make the playground a little bigger.
Put more bins next to the snack shop.
Stop the learners from drinking water.
questions.explanation: Good actions use the evidence. Wrappers come from snacks, so bins near the snack shop (or snacks without wrappers) would help most.

questions.stem: Tuli does a "rubbish diary" at home. Sort each action into reduce, reuse or recycle.
items: taking a water bottle from home instead of buying one
using a jar to store rice
taking newspapers to the bhangari collector
printing on both sides of the paper
giving old clothes to someone else
sending empty glass bottles to be made into new glass
questions.explanation: Reduce means use less. Reuse means use again. Recycle means turning used materials into new things.

questions.stem: Throwing plastic into a drain is harmless because the drain takes it far away.
questions.explanation: Plastic does not rot. It can block drains, cause floods, and end up in rivers and the sea where it harms animals.

questions.stem: A new road will cross a wetland where fish, frogs and birds live. What is the best plan?
options: Cut down all the trees around the wetland.
Fill in the wetland quickly because it is only mud.
Build the road fast and tell nobody about it.
Look for a route that goes round the wetland.
questions.explanation: Filling in wetlands destroys the homes of fish, frogs and birds. A good plan protects the habitat and still meets people's needs.

questions.stem: Class 4A collected 42 pieces of litter: sweet wrappers 18, plastic bottles 7, paper 10, food waste 5, cans 2. Which statement is correct?
options: Paper and cans together were more than the wrappers alone.
Sweet wrappers were less than half of all the litter.
Plastic bottles were the second most common kind of litter.
There were 40 pieces of litter in all, counting everything.
questions.explanation: 18 is less than half of 42 (which is 21). Paper and cans make 12, which is fewer than 18. Paper (10) was second, and the total is 42.

questions.stem: A family uses 5 thin plastic bags every week. They start using one strong jute bag every week instead. How many plastic bags do they avoid in a year of 52 weeks?
options: 52 bags
57 bags
260 bags
520 bags
questions.explanation: 5 × 52 = 260 plastic bags a year. One strong jute bag can be used again and again.

questions.stem: Give one way people have helped an ecosystem in Bangladesh and one way people have harmed one. Explain both.
questions.model_answer: Helped: protecting the Sundarbans as a sanctuary lets tigers and deer survive. Harmed: polluting the Buriganga killed fish and made the water unsafe.
questions.explanation: People help by protecting habitats, planting trees and making laws. People harm by polluting, cutting down forests, hunting and overfishing.

questions.stem: Raju says: "Recycling means using something again, like using a jar to store rice." What is wrong with this?
options: That is reusing; recycling means making used materials into new things.
Recycling means using less of something every single day.
Nothing is wrong, because recycling just means using things again and again.
Recycling means throwing things away safely in the right bin.
questions.explanation: Using a jar again is reusing. Recycling changes used paper, glass, metal or plastic into new things.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper compares thin plastic bags and jute bags. Which statements are fair? Choose all that are right.
options: Jute bags rot away naturally in a few months.
Plastic bags are cheap and light.
Jute bags can be reused many times.
Plastic bags rot away in a few months.
Jute is made from oil.
questions.explanation: Plastic bags are cheap but last hundreds of years. Jute is a plant fibre that rots away and can be reused. Plastic, not jute, comes from oil.
